voice-branch-jargon.notes: [EXPIRED-NO-FIELD-HASH] Fixed. The "### CI enforcement" heading is now "### Validation" and the warn-only / --strict / --strict-wired CI modes and the witness-pipeline.yml reference are gone; what the validator actually checks (dual fields present on every LP/SDP/operator-selection witness) is kept, as is the validator script citation. "enforced in CI" is dropped from the opening. The closing Notes no longer instruct a maintainer to run the validator and no longer call the paper "the corpus"; they now state plainly that not every LP/SDP witness yet carries its dual and that no count is quoted because it changes. The 58-of-58 historical figure is untouched.

trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Full read of alg:lp-sdp-dual-emission. No constructions from the ten categories; zero spaced em-dashes. VERIFIED the six required dual fields against the AGENTS.md contract - y0_star, y_star, active_set, primal_obj, dual_obj, duality_gap - they match exactly, as does the historical '58 of 58' figure. Good discipline worth naming: the Notes deliberately decline to quote a current outstanding count, which is precisely what the corpus rule asks for.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: NOT A TRAP, reported separately: the block names tools/pyhecke/python/pyhecke/lp_dual_solver.py as the canonical entry point, while AGENTS.md names computations/lp_dual_solver.py. BOTH FILES EXIST AND THEIR CONTENTS DIFFER (md5 5c66b818... vs ed28cd38...), so there are two divergent copies of a solver the corpus calls canonical, and this block and AGENTS.md point at different ones.
